correctness.rationale: The two equivalence relations each with two-element classes and singleton intersections define a simple bipartite incidence graph whose E- and F-class vertices each have degree two. Every component is an even alternating cycle with 2k edges (k>=2). Isomorphism types at n=2t correspond exactly to partitions of t into parts >=2, count p(t)-p(t-1). Joint E,F atomic neighbourhood counts at every x equal (1,1,1,n-3) so 1-WL remains uniform; explicit C² sentences enforce n, both class-size-two conditions and |E(x)cap F(x)|=1, making the fibre exact relative to arbitrary pairs of equivalences. Side-preserving automorphisms are edge-transitive within each cycle length and can permute like components; vertex-orbit count equals number distinct partition parts. First unequal sizes (2,3) at t=5 yields n=10 orbit sizes 4,6. Distinct-part minimal weight d(d+3)/2 gives sharp D(n)=floor((sqrt(4n+9)-3)/2) with constructive extremizers. Independent partition enumeration through t=27 plus inspected side-coloured graph isomorphism and first-orbit automorphism scripts support boundaries without substituting for proof.
residual_risks: Only pure two-equivalence signature and matching class size 2; no theorem for higher class sizes or additional relation symbols.
